newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ endorses hefty monetary policy easing.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ endorses hefty monetary policy easing.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand in its six-monthly Monetary Policy Statement on Friday said it wanted monetary conditions the equivalent of 100 basis points easier than it set in its March Economic Projections.
The bank projected its nominal Monetary Conditions Index, which was given an arbitrary December quarter base of 1000, to average 825 over the September quarter.
The index, constructed from a composite of interest rates and the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index, is seen moving to 785 in the December quarter and to 808 in the March 1998 quarter.
According to the bank's desired conditions set in March of bank bills at 7.5 percent and the TWI at 68.0 set in March, the MCI was at 925.
A 100 point move in the MCI is equivalent to a 100 basis point move in 90-day bank bills or a two percent change in the TWI.
Brash said the RBNZ now sees 90-day bank bills averaging 7.0 percent in the September quarter and the TWI at 67.3.

The RBNZ said it expected underlying inflation of 0.3 percent in the June quarter, remaining flat at that level in the September and December 1997 quarters. Core inflation is then picked to drop to 0.1 percent in the March 1998 quarter.
In annual terms, underlying inflation is expected to be 1.0 percent in the March 1998 year, and at 1.1 and 1.7 percent for the succeeding March years.
